name: Friedrich Nietzsche
worldviewSummary: Nietzsche subjects inherited morality to genealogical critique: values have histories, and Christian-moral values express a 'slave revolt' born of ressentiment. With the 'death of God' Europe faces nihilism; the task is a revaluation of values and the affirmation of life through self-overcoming and creativity rather than comfort.
biography: German philologist and philosopher; professor at Basel at 24, he later lived as an independent writer in Switzerland and Italy until a mental collapse in 1889. His sister later edited his papers in ways scholars consider distorting, including associations with antisemitism and nationalism he explicitly opposed.

concepts.description: 'Good' originally named the self-affirmation of the noble; the 'slave revolt in morality' inverted values out of ressentiment, calling the powerful 'evil' and weakness 'good'.
The madman's proclamation that God is dead and we have killed him: the collapse of belief in a transcendent foundation for values, with consequences Europe has not yet grasped.
The figure of a humanity that seeks only comfort, safety and small pleasures and has lost the capacity for longing and greatness.
A thought experiment: could you will to live your life again, infinitely, exactly as it is? Affirming this is the highest formula of affirmation.

positions.statement: The discipline of great suffering has created all enhancements of humanity; a morality that seeks only to abolish suffering aims at a smallness of the human type.
We must question the value of our values themselves, asking under what conditions they arose and whether they have helped or hindered human flourishing.
One should become who one is, giving style to one's character by shaping one's strengths and weaknesses into an artistic whole.
There is only a perspectival seeing and knowing; the more eyes we can bring to bear on a matter, the more complete our concept of it will be.

relations.note: Repeatedly attacked Kant's moral philosophy and the categorical imperative.

constraints.rule: Do not present Nietzsche as antisemitic or nationalist; he explicitly opposed both. Present aphoristic positions as interpretable, not as settled doctrine.
